title: Kotosoupa Avgolemono
subtitle: Greek chicken and rice soup with egg and lemon
excerpt: A whole chicken simmered into a deep golden broth, served with rice and finished with the classic egg and lemon sauce. The Greek soup for when everything else has failed you.
sourceNotes: One of the most familiar dishes in the Greek home kitchen. Synthesised from multiple Greek home cook sources.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the broth and shred the chicken up to 2 days ahead. Reheat the broth, add the rice and make the avgolemono fresh when you are ready to serve.

content.text: Kotosoupa avgolemono starts with a proper whole chicken broth. The quality of the soup depends on that broth, so simmer it long and skim it well. The avgolemono must go in off the heat or the eggs will set into threads.
Put the whole chicken in a large pot. Cover with cold water by about 5cm. Add the onion, carrot, celery, bay leaves, peppercorns and salt.
Bring to the boil over a high heat. Skim off the foam that rises to the top. Reduce to a gentle simmer.
Simmer for 75 to 80 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the broth is golden and flavourful.
Lift out the chicken and set it aside to cool slightly. Strain the broth through a fine sieve into a clean pot. Discard the vegetables.
Bring the broth to a simmer. Add the rinsed rice and cook for 15 minutes until tender. Remove from the heat.
Shred the chicken into pieces, discarding skin and bones. Set aside.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks. Add the yolks and whisk in. Add the lemon juice and whisk again. Slowly ladle 3 scoops of hot broth into the egg mixture, whisking constantly.
Pour the egg mixture back into the pot of soup while stirring. Do not return to the boil. Add the shredded chicken, taste for seasoning, and serve with parsley scattered over.

items.symptom: The avgolemono sauce has curdled into threads.
items.cause: The soup was still boiling when the egg mixture was added, or the tempering was too fast.
items.fix: Always take the pot off the heat completely before adding the avgolemono. Add the hot broth to the eggs one ladle at a time and whisk between each.

items.cause: The water was not skimmed at the start, or it boiled rather than simmered.
items.fix: Skim the foam diligently in the first 10 minutes. Keep the heat low so it barely trembles; a rolling boil makes the broth murky.

items.symptom: The rice has soaked up all the broth.
items.cause: The rice was left sitting in the hot soup too long before serving.
items.fix: Serve the soup as soon as the avgolemono is stirred in. If making ahead, cook the rice separately and add to each bowl at serving.
